frozen_experiment.checker_replay_verdict: ACCEPTED: ALL 20/20 CASES MATCH (exact scores + predicted class)
frozen_experiment.rtl_vs_native_agreement: 20/20 -- all four integer scores and the predicted class are bit-for-bit identical between the RTL-simulated processor and the native TFLM oracle for every one of the 20 fixed comparison cases
frozen_experiment.critical_distinction: 20/20 RTL-vs-native agreement is NOT classifier accuracy. The processor exactly reproduces the model's output -- including the model's own mistakes. Classifier quality (16/20 on these fixed cases; 76.96% accuracy / 0.77093 macro-F1 on the full 599-sample test split, below the unmet 0.85 target) is a separate, independently measured claim.

remaining_limitations: Classifier quality target (macro-F1 >= 0.85) was not met (measured 0.77093).
Only one accepted end-to-end RTL run (full20_final_001) exists; no repeated-run reliability claim is made.
Processor verification used a from-scratch Python ISA reference model, not Spike/Sail (Spike installed but non-functional on this host).
No synthesis, timing closure, FPGA/silicon result -- RTL simulation only; simulated cycle counts are not physical-chip latency.

The chat app's local LLM (1.5B parameters) occasionally exhibits small-model generation artifacts (e.g. a minor word substitution observed in the Spanish transcript captured in this bundle) -- citations/evidence remain the authoritative source, not the LLM's prose.
Knowledge-base retrieval is TF-IDF-based, not semantic/embedding-based; coverage is verified by test but not exhaustive for arbitrary phrasing.
